About Snorkel

Snorkel AI is the frontier AI data lab, helping teams build the data and environments behind high-performing frontier and agentic AI. We combine technology with research-driven AI data development to create datasets, benchmarks, evals, and custom solutions for real-world AI systems. Founded out of the Stanford AI Lab in 2019, Snorkel works with leading AI labs and enterprises to move from better data to better outcomes. 

Excited to help us redefine how AI is built? Apply to be the newest Snorkeler!

About the Role

Snorkel AI is hiring Forward Deployed Researchers (Multiple levels) who will partner with frontier AI labs on their most challenging data problems. This is a high-impact, customer-facing role that combines deep technical and research credibility with the ability to work directly with customer research teams. You'll partner with customer research teams to design complex data and environments that improve frontier model performance, serving as a thought partner throughout the engagement.

You'll work at the critical intersection of research, technical strategy, and customer partnership. This includes scoping training data needs, designing RL environments and tasks, developing evaluation frameworks, probing model behavior and failure modes, and translating customer research objectives into actionable technical plans.

Forward Deployed Researchers own a technical domain. You are the person who knows where frontier models fail in it, what data moves those numbers, and what we should build next.

Main Responsibilities

  • Own a technical domain end to end: the technical bar for what we build in it, and what we build next
  • Partner with frontier AI research labs to design datasets and environments that improve model performance
  • Lead technical conversations with customer researchers to understand model capabilities, failure modes, data requirements, and success criteria
  • Probe model behavior through systematic evaluation to uncover weaknesses and identify high-impact data interventions
  • Benchmark frontier models against our datasets to demonstrate value to customers, building or adapting evaluation harnesses as needed, and turn the results into pass-rate analysis, failure-mode breakdowns, and purchase recommendations
  • Design evaluation frameworks, calibration processes, and quality rubrics that establish measurable project success metrics
  • Develop technical specifications for data projects that balance research rigor with operational feasibility
  • Hold the demand shape for your domain: which labs want what, at what volume, against what bar, and where the asks are converging
  • Develop a point of view on where your domain is heading, and partner with Research on what should exist before a customer asks for it
  • Serve as thought partner to customer research teams throughout the sales cycle, building trust and credibility
  • Stay current on frontier AI research, RL environment design, post-training techniques, and evaluation methodologies

Preferred Qualifications

  • Strong expertise in frontier AI concepts including LLMs, training data pipelines, evaluation methodologies, post-training techniques (RLHF, DPO, RLAIF), and domain areas such as coding agents, reasoning, multimodal models, or RL environments
  • Experience in applied ML research, data science, or research-intensive technical roles
  • Customer-facing or collaborative research experience, or demonstrated aptitude for client engagement
  • Proficiency in Python, familiarity with ML frameworks and LLM APIs, and comfort running evaluations in containerized environments
  • Excellent communication skills, ability to deliver technical presentations and explain

Technical Accounting

Financial Reporting

  • Prepare audit-ready workpapers and accounting schedules.

jobs.title: Principal Place and Route (PnR) Engineer
jobs.location: Austin, Texas, United States; San Jose, California, United States
jobs.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the team

The Place and Route team writes the software that maps dataflow graphs onto SambaNova’s Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit (RDU). Our tools partition each graph, place the pieces on the chip’s compute and memory units, and route the communication between them. The quality of that mapping sets the throughput of the compiled program, including large language model inference and training. We are looking to grow our team with highly motivated engineers who want to utilize advanced algorithms to solve challenging problems. 

About the Role

You will develop and tune the partitioning, placement, and routing algorithms that map customer workloads onto the RDU. You will work with the compiler team, hardware architects, and performance engineers to model new hardware constraints and trace throughput gaps back to mapping decisions. Your changes will ship in production releases and show up in measured performance.

Responsibilities

  • Develop partitioning, placement, and routing algorithms that meet hardware resource constraints and keep compile times practical
  • Tune PnR results for target workloads, including LLM inference at different batch sizes and concurrency levels
  • Model new hardware constraints and architecture features in our solvers and heuristics as the chip evolves
  • Analyze compiled output with performance engineers and trace throughput gaps back to mapping decisions
  • Build the infrastructure for prototyping, regression testing, and deployment of PnR changes
  • Work with the compiler and hardware teams to define interfaces and resource models

Required Qualifications

  • M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related field
  • 3+ years of experience developing optimization or graph algorithms in industry or research
  • Expert knowledge of graph algorithms, partitioning algorithms, combinatorial optimization, or MILP solvers
  • Strong proficiency in C/C++
  • Familiarity with Python
  • Experience designing large, highly parallel, performance-sensitive systems
  • Ability to learn hardware architecture and apply it to improve performance
  • Experience solving NP-hard problems in practice with heuristics, approximation, or pruned exact methods

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with place and route for FPGAs, CGRAs, or other spatial architectures
  • Experience with ML compilers such as MLIR, LLVM, TVM, or XLA
  • Experience with simulated annealing, constraint programming, or SAT/SMT solvers
  • Familiarity with LLM inference stacks such as vLLM and PyTorch
  • Publications at venues such as FPGA, DAC, ICCAD, or MLSys

 

Base Salary Range:

jobs.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the team

We take frontier open-weight models (dense, mixture-of-experts with hundreds of experts, hybrid Mamba/attention, sliding-window attention, multi-token prediction) from Hugging Face to production serving on SambaNova's RDU dataflow accelerators. That means compiling them, proving them numerically correct against the reference, serving them with the full feature set, and merging the work into a shared stack so the next model is cheaper.

About the role

You will bring new open-weight LLMs, including dense, mixture-of-experts, and hybrid Mamba/attention architectures, up on SambaNova’s RDU dataflow accelerators and into production serving. That means adapting the model, mapping it across chips and hosts, compiling it, and validating it numerically against the reference. You also build inference features like continuous batching, speculative decoding, and FP8/FP4 as shared modules, so each new model costs less to bring up.

 

Responsibilities

  • Bring up new LLM architectures end to end: model adaptation, checkpoint conversion, multi-chip / multi-host mapping, compile, strict numerical validation, production serving with latency / throughput numbers.
  • Build inference features once as shared modules: continuous batching over a paged KV pool, prompt caching, chunked and incremental prefill, dynamic tensor shapes, speculative decoding (EAGLE-3, drafters, MTP), FP8 / FP4, tensor and expert parallelism.
  • Debug where model, compiler and hardware meet; land each fix in the right shared component.

Required qualifications

  • B.S. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or related field
  • 8+ years of industry experience in ML systems, inference, or compiler engineering
  • Strong Python and PyTorch internals experience, plus some C++
  • Deep transformer-inference knowledge, including KV caching, GQA and sliding window attention, MoE routing, prefill vs decode, batching, and speculative decoding
  • Hands-on experience with accelerator bring-up, ML compilers (MLIR, XLA, TVM, Triton, torch-mlir), or inference engines (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM)
  • Rigor in numerical debugging
  • Comfort with Bazel, Slurm, and large monorepos
  • Clear writing and evidence-backed claims

Preferred qualifications

  • M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or related field
  • Experience with dataflow or spatial compilers
  • Experience with kernel DSLs
  • Experience with FP8 and FP4 inference
  • Experience with Mamba and SSMs

 - ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

 - ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

HOW WE WORK

 - High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

 - Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

 - AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

 - Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

 - Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

 - Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

 - Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

 - Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

 - Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role
We build AI-powered engines that make, localize, launch and learn from creative, using ElevenLabs’ full audio and video stack. Enterprise customers are already working with us. While our product teams focus on self-serve, these roles seed a dedicated enterprise engineering team: the people who make ElevenCreative work for our biggest customers and unblock enterprise deals. You sit between the customer and the product. You’ll talk to enterprise customers, understand their requirements, and decide whether to build a bespoke integration for them or a product improvement for everyone. Making that call well is the job.


Requirements

Bonus: experience with localization or TMS integrations, brand or marketing tooling, or adtech.

jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

SECURITY ENGINEER, KUBERNETES

We protect the platform that runs X and SpaceXSI. We don’t just report issues, we actively look for real risks and exploits in our Kubernetes environments and turn them into durable fixes and tooling. You will secure the platform behind X and SpaceXSI’s infrastructure, products, and workloads. If you know pod and platform security, think in attack paths, and want to build the defenses that make the platform safer at scale, we want to hear from you.

We value a understanding of how Kubernetes can actually be abused – not just how it is configured. We prioritize shipping practical controls and tooling over writing policy documents, applying least privilege and defense-in-depth at fleet scale, delivering clear findings and fixes that platform teams can act on, and conducting safe, constrained validation that does not put production at risk.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Secure the platform end to end: nodes, clusters, pods, roles, tokens, secrets, service-to-service communication, and the supply chain
  • Find and remediate overprivileged permissions, dangerous pod and workload settings, and escalation paths in operators, admission, networking, identity, and monitoring
  • Assess our own platform the way an adversary would, including container and pod breakout, privilege escalation, and movement across workloads, using safe and constrained validation, then fix what you find
  • Design and build security tooling and automation, including AI-assisted analysis, that catches risky configuration and overprivilege before or after it ships
  • Strengthen identity and secrets handling so workloads receive only the access they need
  • Improve supply-chain security through secure base images, continuous scanning, and related controls
  • Review changes that affect RBAC, operators, ServiceAccounts, network policies, and anything running with elevated privileges
  • Partner with platform and product teams as a security owner, taking problems from identification through rollout
  • Contribute to fleet-wide hardening, policy enforcement, and safer defaults

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 3+ years in platform security, Kubernetes security, or offensive security against production infrastructure

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Deep knowledge of pod and workload security: privileged containers, capabilities, host namespaces, host path mounts, service accounts, RBAC, admission control, and network isolation
  • Working knowledge of identity, secrets, workload identity, service-to-service trust, supply chain, runtime, and cloud access
  • Able to think like an attacker, measure blast radius, and turn the path into a detection, control, or tool
  • Comfortable with operators, custom resources, Helm, and GitOps workflows
  • Able to build or modify security tooling in Go, Python, or Rust when a control needs automation
  • Bonus: Image scanning, SBOMs, secure base images, policy-as-co

jobs.description:
About Us

Firefly Neuroscience builds technology that helps improve how brain health careis delivered. Our technology focuses on making high-quality brain insights moreaccessible to clinicians and, ultimately, to the patients who depend on timely andaccurate care.

Make sure to read the full description below, and please apply immediately if you are confident you meet all the requirements.

By bringing greater objectivity and consistency to brain assessment, we helpreduce uncertainty in clinical decision-making and support more efficient pathsfrom evaluation to treatment. The goal is simple: clearer information, fewer delays,and better experiences for patients navigating complex care systems.

We are a growing team that values thoughtful problem-solving, high standards,and work that has real-world impact. If you are interested in contributing totechnology that meaningfully improves care while being built with care, Fireflyoffers the opportunity to do work that matters.

Role Summary

Firefly Neuroscience is hiring a Lead Data Scientist to own the neuroscience behind every number on our reports and to build what comes next. Our platform turns clinical EEG recordings into measures and reports that clinicians use in psychiatry and neurology practices. You will inherit that pipeline, verify it, and make it defensible; build and ship machine-learning models on real clinical data; and lay the groundwork for foundation models trained on neural data.

This is a hands-on, high-ownership role in a small, senior team. The science isyours end to end: you set the methodology, you ship in Python inside theengineering process, and you are the scientific authority our clinical advisors andcustomers rely on - with the Tech Lead, our clinical advisor, and companyleadership as direct partners. EEG expertise is not required - depth in neural orclinical data is. If your background is MRI or another modality, you will beexpected to come up to speed on EEG quickly.

Key Responsibilities
• Build, validate, deploy, and monitor machine-learning models on real clinicaldata - biomarker models, calibrated replacements for rules-based logic, andthe foundations for models trained at scale on our EEG corpus.
• Own the measures. For every number on a Firefly report, own what it is, how itis computed, what reference it is compared against, and its documentedlimitations.
• Verify and strengthen the existing analysis pipeline: reproduce and auditinherited methods, set acceptance criteria before comparisons, and fix whatdoes not hold up - with evidence that would stand up to clinical and regulatoryreview.
• Build and maintain the normative reference data our reports compare patientsagainst: reference population definition, covariate adjustment (age, sex), z-score construction, sample-size adequacy, and a process for refreshingnorms as data accumulates.
• Deliver sponsored-research analyses for external partners on time and to astandard that survives peer review, stating plainly what a sample can andcannot support.
• Partner with the Tech Lead on delivery and with our clinical advisor on clinicaldirection; ship through the engineering team's process, including changecontrol for any change to a measure or norm on the product.

Qualifications

Required
• 8+ years in a data science role.
• Master's degree or higher - or equivalent sustained hands-on research orindustry experience - in neuroscience, neuroimaging, clinical neurophysiology,biomedical engineering, or a closely related field, with enough depth to reasonindependently about what a brain measure reflects physiologically and whereit breaks down.
• Demonstrated experience building, shipping, and maintaining machine-learning or statistical models on neural or clinical data (EEG, MRI, or otherneuroimaging or physiological modalities), including sound handling of smallsamples, leakage, and class imbalance.
• Hands-on experience building and validating normative or reference datasets:defining reference populations

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!

Why this role?

Are you energized by bridging the gap between frontier AI capability and complex customer reality? Do you want to architect high-performance, resilient machine learning systems directly inside strategic enterprise environments? We are looking for a Staff Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to join our team. The team is responsible for taking our large language models and making them work reliably, securely, and at peak performance within our customers' custom infrastructure and data perimeters.

In this role, you will act as the principal technical translation layer between our core engineering teams and our strategic partners. You will own the architecture for highly ambiguous, customer-specific inference challenges—ranging from multi-tenant model serving to multi-datacenter disaster recovery and custom hardware validation. You will lead technical adoption end-to-end, ensuring our models achieve exceptionally low latency, high throughput, and seamless resilience in the field.



As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you will:

• Embed directly with customer engineering teams to architect the "connective tissue" between our AI models and their live, complex production environments.

• Design advanced model serving topologies, implementing multi-tenant architectures, intelligent model routing, and cross-datacenter failover strategies for multi-cluster environments.

• Optimize "AI-in-a-box" and private deployments, balancing localized SRE constraints like Kubernetes multi-cluster scale with raw model performance.

• Conduct rigorous benchmarking and profiling of customer LLM workloads, root-causing performance degradation (e.g., slow generation) via metrics, dashboards, and distributed logs.

• Accelerate hardware validation, collaborating with clients to run and support Cohere models on next-generation accelerators (GPUs, TPUs, AMD, and custom ASICs).

• Translate complex field friction into platform upgrades, delivering prescriptive feedback and contributing directly back to core product features.

• Ensure Day-1 production reliability, assisting customers in establishing sound deployment patterns, SLOs, and observability frameworks.



You may be a good fit if you have:

• 8+ years of engineering experience running production infrastructure, designing large-scale distributed systems, or deploying enterprise software in complex environments.

• Deep technical depth in production Kubernetes, including orchestration across multi-cluster and hybrid/multi-cloud ecosystems (GCP, Azure, AWS, OCI).

jobs.description:
About Decagon

Decagon is the leading conversational AI platform empowering every brand to deliver concierge customer experiences.

Our technology enables industry-defining enterprises like Avis Budget Group, Block’s Cash App and Square, Chime, Oura Health, and Hunter Douglas to deploy AI agents that power personalized, deeply satisfying interactions across voice, chat, email, SMS, and every other channel.

We’re building a future where customer experiences are being redefined from support tickets and hold music to faster resolutions, richer conversations, and deeper relationships. We’re proud to be backed by world-class investors who share that vision, including a16z, Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, Coatue, and Index Ventures, along with many others.

We’re an in-office company, driven by a shared commitment to excellence and velocity. Our values — Just Get It Done, Invent What Customers Want, Winner’s Mindset, and The Polymath Principle — shape how we work and grow as a team.



About the Team

Data Lifecycle at Decagon builds the systems that govern how sensitive customer data is handled throughout its lifetime: what we store, who can access it, how we redact it, and when we delete it. We turn complex privacy requirements into reliable infrastructure and product that customers can configure and trust.

This team is core to how Decagon scales. Our AI agents work with sensitive information across conversations, tool calls, and customer systems. The frameworks we build need to protect that data consistently across the platform, while preserving the context customers need to operate and improve their agents. A failure mode we debug in production becomes a guardrail, a test, or a piece of tooling that catches it everywhere.

Our systems run for companies like Hertz, American Airlines, and Notion across chat, voice, email, and SMS.



About the Role

You’ll design and build the platform infrastructure that let customers control how their data is collected, retained, redacted, and deleted. That means strong engineering underneath, and clear abstractions on top that hold up across different enterprise requirements without forking per customer.

You’ll work day to day with product management, governance, and security: understanding customer requirements, defining data handling guarantees, reviewing designs, and iterating through launch. You’ll stay close enough to customers to understand their privacy and operational needs in depth and to ensure what you’re building is actually right for them.

Engineers here own features end to end, from technical architecture through deployment and the iteration after it. On this team, that includes verifying that sensitive data is protected and the action actually completes. An understanding of durable and fault-tolerant systems is key.



In this role, you will

 - Build PII handling and redaction systems that identify and protect sensitive information across conversations, agent traces, and other customer data

 - Design configuration abstractions for redaction and retention policies that balance enterprise flexibility with clear, safe defaults

 - Build reliable data deletion workflows that propagate across storage systems and derived data, with retries, verification, and visibility into failures

 - Build self-serve tools and APIs that let customers configure, test, and understand their data lifecycle policies without relying on an engineer

 - Build LLM-backed systems that scan and detect data anomalies and violations

 - Train and/or tune models for detecting data of various forms (including PII and PHI)

 - Extend redaction and identification to multimodal agents, including images, attachments, voice notes, and documents.

 - Build monitoring and auditability that make it clear what data was processed, what remains, and where a policy has failed—without exposing sensitive information in the process

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Safety
jobs.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD


At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.



About the role 

This is Bedrock's first dedicated Safety Technical Program Manager, a role built to establish the execution structure that lets us roll out new autonomy capabilities quickly without compromising safety rigor. As we scale to new machine types and expanded operational domains, we are evolving our safety practices toward more explicit, strategic execution.

You will own program execution for the safety, systems engineering, and state estimation work that makes autonomous heavy equipment safe to operate in the real world. This is a hands-on individual contributor role driving alignment and delivery across engineering, safety, autonomy, hardware, and field operations through influence, structure, and clear communication. You will be the connective tissue between safety strategy and technical delivery, making sure requirements are traceable, dependencies are visible, and risks surface early enough to act on. We are a startup that values agility. We believe that speed and safety are compatible when the traceability behind them is solid.



What you'll do

 - Own planning and strategic execution for the safety and systems portions of the autonomy roadmap, from requirements through validated field deployment.

 - Support safety requirements being traceable, reusable across platforms and sites, and integrated into roadmaps from inception, partnering with safety and systems engineering on hazard analysis, validation evidence, and release readiness.

 - Build and maintain the validation plan spanning simulation and on-site testing, ensuring system-level changes are verified before they reach customers.

 - Map and actively manage dependencies and tradeoffs across systems, hardware, software, state estimation, and safety, weighing safety impact alongside schedule impact and identifying single points of failure on the critical path before they slip.

 - Drive program reviews, risk, and change management for multi-disciplinary, safety-critical initiatives, and provide reporting on roadmap health, delivery status, and safety implications clear enough to support both executive decisions and customer-facing discussions.

 - Translate field signals into prioritized engineering work and tracking issues to resolution.



What you'll bring

 - 7+ years of technical program management experience, including 2+ years leading programs involving safety-critical or high-integrity systems.

 - Domain experience in robotics, autonomous systems, aerospace, or another physical-world safety-critical domain, with a working understanding of the software, firmware, and hardware stacks behind real-world autonomy.

 - Working familiarity with a functional safety standard, such as ISO 26

Our Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) don't advise from the sidelines. PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

 - Debugging model failures in production AI systems

 - Scoping six- and seven-figure technical engagements with Sales and presenting them to C-suite and engineering leadership buyers

 - Enabling GSI or consulting partners to deliver technical engagements

A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSEs) work directly with customers to quickly understand their greatest problems and design and implement solutions to use data against them. Whether you aspire to be an entrepreneur or an engineering leader, we believe Palantir is the best place — with the best colleagues — to learn how. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the Team

The Cloud Platform team owns the production inferencing service that serves SambaNova's models to customers on RDU accelerators, including capacity planning, deployment, monitoring, and incident response across regions in the United States, Asia, Europe, and Latin America.

About the Role

As a Principal Cloud Platform Engineer, you will specialize in our AI Inferencing Service and be the guardian of its reliability, performance, and scalability. You will bridge the gap between software development and operations, applying an engineering mindset to solve operational challenges. Your primary focus will be ensuring our inference endpoints have exceptional uptime, low-latency response times, and efficient resource utilization, directly impacting the experience of our customers and the success of our AI products. This role includes participating in a shared on-call rotation to maintain 24/7 service reliability.

Responsibilities

  • Shared ownership of the production inferencing service across regions, covering availability, latency, performance, change management, and capacity planning
  • Standing up and automating AI infrastructure in new regions
  • Participating in a shared primary/secondary on-call rotation, and leading incident response
  • Building monitoring, alerting, and dashboards in Prometheus, Grafana, and Datadog for service health, model latency and throughput, and accelerator utilization
  • Finding and eliminating performance bottlenecks
  • Designing auto-scaling policies that handle variable inference loads
  • Managing cloud and on-prem infrastructure as code in Terraform and Ansible
  • Building CI/CD pipelines that safely deploy new model versions and service updates
  • Forecasting infrastructure needs against the product roadmap and usage trends, and working with finance to manage cloud spend
  • Defining and reporting on SLOs and SLIs for the inferencing platform, using that data to prioritize reliability work

Required Qualifications

  • B.S. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related field
  • 8+ years of experience in Site Reliability Engineering, DevOps, or related roles
  • Experience supporting a large-scale, customer-facing service in a public cloud environment (AWS, GCP, Azure)
  • Strong programming and scripting skills in languages like Python, Go, Rust, or Java
  • Proven experience with containerization and orchestration technologies (Docker and Kubernetes)
  • Deep understanding of monitoring and observability principles and tools (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, ELK Stack, Datadog)
  • Experience with Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform, CloudFormation)
  • Experience with CI/CD principles and tools (e.g., Jenkins, GitHub Actions, ArgoCD)
  • Strong Linux/Unix system administration fundamentals

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in a hybrid environment bridging cloud and on-premise/data center infrastructure
  • Direct experience supporting ML/AI inferencing services in production

About the role

The Data team at SpaceXSI is a small team that works across the company to inform business and product decisions, and we’re hiring the first member of our team to focus fully on marketing. Performance Marketing at SpaceXSI drives scaled acquisition across 10+ channels for Grok, Grok Bot, and our full portfolio of AI products, across consumer, SMB, startup, and enterprise audiences.

This role will sit in the central Data team and partner directly with Marketing leadership to own the measurement and analysis of performance marketing, growth marketing programs, and overall marketing measurement. What you'll do

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (Site Reliability Engineer, Cloud Infrastructure)
jobs.description:
Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month. Every answer, every Perplexity Computer task, and every enterprise deployment runs on production infrastructure owned by the Cloud Infrastructure team: a fleet of Kubernetes clusters across a multi-account AWS estate, private networks that reach hyperscalers and the neoclouds serving our models, and the storage underneath our user data and agentic workloads. We're looking for SREs who treat reliability as a software problem. You'll own compute, networking, and storage at scale and keep production stable while everything built on top of it is changing fast.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own production at scale. Run the compute, networking, and storage foundation behind Perplexity's consumer, Computer, API, and enterprise products, and own its availability, latency, and cost.

 - Run our Kubernetes fleet. Operate and upgrade the EKS clusters that host web services, search, datastores, and secure sandboxes. Tune scheduling, autoscaling, node lifecycle, DNS, and service networking so clusters stay healthy under bursty, fast-growing load.

 - Engineer the network. Design and operate VPC architectures, Transit Gateway and PrivateLink connectivity, load balancing, DNS, and egress across accounts, regions, and cloud providers.

 - Keep data durable and fast. Own the storage layer (EBS, S3, DynamoDB, and the managed databases and caches our services depend on), including performance, durability, backups, and restores that have actually been tested.

 - Manage everything as code. Run infrastructure through Terraform and CI/CD. Build reusable modules and guardrails, and make every change reviewable, repeatable, and safe to roll back.

 - Prepare for failures. Define SLOs, build alerts that someone can act on, design for zone and regional failure, and run game days and disaster-recovery exercises that prove recovery works.

 - Lead incident response. Be on the critical path when things break. Drive incidents to resolution, write blameless postmortems, and land the fixes so the same failure never pages anyone twice.

 - Scale ahead of demand. Own capacity planning, quotas, reservations, and cost efficiency so product launches and traffic spikes never wait on infrastructure.

 - Automate away the toil. Build tooling, increasingly agent-driven, that turns provisioning, upgrades, and remediation into self-serve, hands-off workflows for every engineering team.




QUALIFICATIONS

We expect you to have real depth in most of these:

 - Deep AWS expertise. You know VPC, IAM, EC2, EKS, ELB, Route 53, S3, EBS, etc. well past the console, including their limits, failure modes, and the bill that comes with them.

 - Production Kubernetes at scale: cluster upgrades, CNI, CoreDNS, autoscalers like Karpenter, and debugging a misbehaving node at 3 a.m. Writing Helm charts alone doesn't count.

 - Terraform mastery. You've designed module structures, managed state across many accounts, and run large refactors and imports without taking production down.

 - Strong networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, load balancing, routing).

 - You write real code in Python, Go, or Rust for automation, tooling, and controllers, and you'd rather automate a runbook than follow it.

 - Fluency with observability tools like Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana, and the judgment to turn metrics, logs, and traces into SLOs and alerts that matter.

 - A track record of leading production incidents and turning root-cause analysis into durable fixes.

 - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you.




ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE

 - Multi-region active-active or failover architectures, and disaster-recovery programs with real recovery targets.

 - Proxies, service meshes, and kernel-level networking: Envoy, Istio, Cilium, or eBPF.

 - GitOps and progressive delivery: Argo CD, Flux, or similar.

 - Enterprise and compliance environments: single-tenant or BYOC deployments, KMS/BYOK,

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, GPU Cluster Infrastructure)
jobs.description:
Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month, and every one of them fans out into multiple AI inference requests running in real time. Behind that sits a large GPU fleet spread across several cloud providers. Today, our inference engineers and researchers build models while also managing networking, securing capacity, and operating the underlying GPU clusters, responsibilities we want a dedicated platform team to own. Your job is to take ownership of that infrastructure and hide its complexity behind a unified, self-serve platform for running training and inference workloads.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Build a self-serve compute platform. Design and own the systems that let inference engineers and researchers launch training jobs and operate inference services without managing GPU provisioning, cluster configuration, or provider-specific infrastructure.

 - Operate the GPU fleet. Own provisioning, lifecycle management, reliability, and capacity integration across providers, giving teams a consistent way to use compute regardless of where it runs.

 - Solve for GPU scarcity. Build the scheduling and placement logic that finds available capacity across providers, packs it efficiently, and gets the right workload onto the right hardware under real constraints.

 - Support two very different workloads. Keep long-running distributed training jobs healthy while simultaneously guaranteeing the availability and latency of production inference services on the same fleet.

 - Own the Kubernetes for GPU orchestration. Write the operators and CRDs, and manage many clusters across providers so the platform behaves the same everywhere we run.

 - Make failure boring. Build the fault tolerance, autoscaling, and observability that keep the fleet utilized and let workloads survive node loss, provider hiccups, and capacity shifts without human intervention.

 - Set technical direction across teams. Partner with inference and cloud infrastructure engineers to turn operational constraints into a coherent platform architecture and roadmap.




QUALIFICATIONS

We expect you to have real depth in most of these:

 - Deep Kubernetes experience — custom operators, CRDs, and multi-cluster federation, not just running kubectl apply.

 - You've managed GPU clusters at scale: NVIDIA hardware, CUDA, and the networking that makes them fast (InfiniBand or RoCE).

 - You've orchestrated compute across multiple clouds (CoreWeave, AWS, GCP, or similar) and understand how different each one really is.

 - Strong distributed systems fundamentals: scheduling, resource allocation, and fault tolerance under load.

 - You write infrastructure and systems-level code in Go, Rust or C++.

 - You've supported both long-running training jobs and high-availability inference services, and you know why they pull infrastructure in opposite directions.

 - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you.




ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE

 - Inference serving stacks: vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM.

 - Slurm or other HPC schedulers.

 - GPU kernel work in CUDA or Triton — not required, but notable.

 - High-speed interconnects: InfiniBand, RoCE, or RDMA in production.

 - Observability for ML workloads: Prometheus, Grafana, or Weights & Biases.

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.

The opportunity

Build AI agents that carry meaningful work from intent to a verified outcome, not merely produce an impressive response. You will engineer the execution loops, tools, context, permissions, evaluations, and runtime controls that let agents operate across complex workflows while remaining understandable, steerable, and safe when systems or assumptions fail.

This role sits where applied AI, distributed systems, and product engineering meet. You will work on long-running behavior, real enterprise integrations, and difficult production failures, deciding when a deterministic workflow is enough, when autonomy adds value, and whether each added degree of freedom earns its operational and user-experience cost.

About Challenger

Challenger is a new EY program focused on building the firm’s next generation of services. It pursues opportunities where AI enables a fundamentally different service and way of delivering it, including rethinking existing offerings and developing new ones.

Small, dedicated teams build and test ideas in real conditions. Solutions that demonstrate clear business value and operational readiness transition to the business for adoption and scale.

Challenger Core develops and maintains the shared technology, methods, and risk and quality guardrails that support this work. Each team contributes reusable tools and practices, helping make the next service faster and less costly to build.

Your key responsibilities

• Engineer agent behavior. Shape planning, routing, delegation, stopping, retry, and handoff behavior across complete workflows.

• Make behavior observable. Instrument end-to-end traces and replay so teams can understand failures, diagnose patterns, and turn production evidence into improvements.
• Protect user control. Design clear intervention points so people can inspect, interrupt, redirect, and safely resume agent work.
• Build shared capability. Partner across product, platform, knowledge, security, and evaluation teams and publish reusable agent patterns and operational lessons.

jobs.location: Austin, Texas, United States; San Jose, California, United States
jobs.description:
SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the Team

The compiler team at SambaNova powers the RDU through a unique compilation strategy. By fusing kernels into dataflow graphs that run across the entire accelerator architecture, we avoid sequential kernel launches and eliminate the memory traffic that bottlenecks conventional hardware. This is a key differentiator and unlike any other product on the market. 

About the Role

As a new grad Compiler Engineer, you'll work on core areas of our compiler, including the IR and pass infrastructure, model lowering and partitioning, tensor tiling, memory management, and mapping operations onto the fabric. Compiler and hardware design are closely linked here, and you'll see how compiler decisions affect chip performance. You'll write production code in C++ and Python, debug at a low level, and work with the runtime and hardware teams. Senior engineers will review your code and mentor you as you take on larger parts of the compiler.

Responsibilities

  • Implement and optimize passes in the compiler's IR and pass infrastructure
  • Lower and partition machine learning models for execution on the RDU
  • Develop tensor tiling and memory management for on-chip memory
  • Map operations onto the RDU fabric to improve model performance
  • Debug compiler and performance issues at a low level in C++ and Python

Required Qualifications

  • B.S. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field

jobs.title: Technical Artist
jobs.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD


At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for an exceptional Technical Artist to join our team building and scaling our robotics simulation environment. Simulation is a critical foundation for autonomy at Bedrock—it allows us to validate end-to-end systems, evaluate complex and unsafe scenarios, and run testing at massive scale.

Our autonomy stack is deeply machine-learning–driven, and closing the sim-to-real gap is a core focus of this role. The simulator must accurately represent a living, breathing construction site - real-world lighting, 3D content, and terrain deformation for digging and earthmoving - while remaining efficient enough to support thousands of runs. High-quality simulation directly accelerates robotics development, making this work central to our success.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the 3D content generation and curation pipeline for an autonomous construction simulator

 - Develop simulation systems that support ML-based autonomy, evaluation, and safety validation

 - Improve realism and performance to better reflect real-world behavior

 - Help guide our strategy in procedural scene generation and rendering techniques


WHO YOU ARE

Simulation spans many disciplines, and we don’t expect one person to do everything. Strong candidates typically bring:

 - A passion for large-scale, realistic simulation systems

 - Experience with advanced 3D simulation software

 - A hands-on mindset and enthusiasm for building core simulation content


QUALIFICATIONS

Required

 - Games or simulation background with minimum 4yrs working in real time 3D

 - Strong foundation in technical art: 3D modeling, texturing, rigging, animation, PBR materials, lighting, performance optimization

 - Hands-on experience with Unreal Engine, minimum 2yrs

Preferred

 - Robotics simulation experience

 - Experience with Isaac Sim or Omniverse

 - Experience with neural rendering techniques (Gaussian splats, NeRFs)

Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer

We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic.

AI Engineer III

How you’ll contribute to our mission:

We’re looking for a hands-on AI Engineer to design, build, and ship customer-facing, production-grade features powered by modern LLMs. You’ll partner with product, data, platform, and Customer Experience/Support to turn messy real-world problems into reliable, safe, and measurable AI solutions. You’ll close the loop from voice-of-customer insight → model/design choices → launch → telemetry and iteration, with success measured by outcomes like task completion, CSAT, time-to-resolution, and deflection rate—not just model scores.

You will help develop the next-generation agentic platform that powers customer-facing assistants across the entire journey—from discovery and onboarding to in-product guidance and support. These agents will reason, plan, call internal tools/APIs, retrieve knowledge, and escalate to humans gracefully. You’ll collaborate with CX/Support, Product, and Platform to integrate with CRM and knowledge bases, implement memory and personalization, enforce safety/quality guardrails, and run evaluations and A/B tests. Success is measured in real CX outcomes: shorter time-to-resolution, higher FCR/CSAT, lower effort, and reliable containment.

How you’ll drive success:
• Own end-to-end development of LLM features: problem framing, data prep, prototyping, offline/online evaluation, deployment, and monitoring.
• Build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines with vector search (e.g., FAISS, Pinecone, OpenSearch/KNN) and document orchestration.
• Implement prompt strategies, tool use/function calling, and guardrails for safety, bias, and privacy.
• Integrate models in production services (REST/GraphQL/gRPC), including auth, rate limiting, and observability.
• Stand up evals and experiment frameworks (A/B tests, golden sets, regression suites) with clear success metrics.
• Optimize for latency, cost, and quality: prompt compression, caching, model selection, fine-tuning/LoRA, distillation where appropriate.
• Collaborate with DevOps/MLOps/Platform to automate CI/CD, data/version management, and feature flags.
• Embed with CX/Support to mine tickets, chats, and call transcripts; convert VOC into training/eval datasets and backlog priorities.

• Build feedback loops (thumbs-up/down, rationale capture, escalation) and human-in-the-loop fallbacks that protect quality.
• Own reliability and UX details that matter for customers: latency budgets, safe fallbacks, clear handoff to human agents, accessibility.

• Ship 1–2 LLM features to production with SLAs, monitoring, and rollback plans.
• Establish an eval harness (offline + online) and quality gates for prompts/RAG.

• Create internal runbooks and dashboards for reproducibility and troubleshooting.

• Model customization (fine-tuning/LoRA) and synthetic data generation.

As an Associate Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) at Databricks, you'll be in a hands-on, customer-facing role for builders who thrive at the intersection of technology and business impact. You'll work directly with enterprise customers to build and productionize data & AI solutions on the Databricks platform. This early-career role is ideal for a strong software engineer looking to grow into a technical leader. You will embed with customer teams, ship production-grade systems, and learn the Databricks platform deeply alongside senior FDEs and our engineering organization.

The impact you will have:

  • Production Solution Delivery: Deliver production-grade systems and reference architectures, contributing reusable frameworks, tools, and best practices along the way.

  • Own the Architecture: Contribute to architecture and design decisions for secure, scalable, full-stack solutions on the Databricks platform.
  • Embed with customer teams to understand their technical and business challenges and help deliver measurable impact.
  • Collaborate closely with senior FDEs, Databricks engineering, and customer support to unblock customers and feed learnings back into the product.
  • Manage technical scope and timelines for your workstreams, growing toward end-to-end delivery ownership.
  • Work with the Databricks technical team, Project Manager, Architect and Customer team to ensure the technical components of the engagement are delivered to meet customer's needs.

What we look for:

  • 2+ years of experience in software engineering, data engineering, or data platforms & analytics.
  • Strong full-stack software engineering skills proficiency in Python and JavaScript/TypeScript, and comfort working across back-end services, APIs, and modern front-end frameworks.
  • Solid computer science fundamentals: data structures, algorithms, testing, and version control.
  • Experience with at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP), or a strong desire to develop cloud expertise quickly.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD, and an interest in production data architectures and MLOps, ML/AI models and AI APIs.
  • Excellent communication skills and a genuine interest in customer-facing engineering work.
  • Build skills in technical areas, and demonstrate curiosity, adaptability, and eagerness to explore new technologies which support the deployment and integration of Databricks-based solutions to complete customer projects.
  • Experience with Apache Spark or distributed data processing is a plus. We'll help you build platform depth on the job.
  • Databricks Certification is a plus, and can be obtained after joining.

About Databricks

Databricks is a data and AI company. More than 10,000 organizations worldwide rely on Databricks to unify and democratize data, analytics and AI. Databricks is headquartered in San Francisco, with offices around the globe, and was founded by the original creators of Lakehouse, Apache Spark™, Delta Lake and MLflow.

Recent graduate?: We’d love for you to explore our current internship openings on our careers page and submit your application for our roles designed for new college graduates.

This role is based in our Mountain View, CA office. Travel to customers is expected approximately 20% of the time.

At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

You'll join the New Product Introduction team within SambaNova's hardware operations organization. The team takes AI server systems from prototype through high-volume production at global contract manufacturers, owning manufacturability, test coverage, yield, and quality, and working closely with electrical, mechanical, firmware, and supply chain teams to get each new product built at scale.
